title: Vector and Static Again
premise: Coral Lockridge has spent nine years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony fleet that stopped answering long ago. When a manifest update arrives for the Vector and Static — a ship destroyed before launch — listing her own name as crew, she discovers the fleet's survivors have been rewriting history to hide a mutiny, and that her memories of her sister's death are an implanted cover story. Racing a failing relay at the edge of dead space, she must broadcast the true records before the fleet's fragile truce expires and the surviving ships turn on each other. She reaches the relay in time, but chooses to send the truth anonymously, preserving the truce while sacrificing her own restored identity — survival, she learns, is something you pay for with the self you might have been.
about_author: Jonah Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people left behind by systems that forgot them.

chapters.title: The Quiet Inventory
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She walks the seed vault's frozen corridors, logging germination tests and recording another unanswered transmission to the fleet. The chapter establishes her routines, her loneliness, and her habit of talking to the seeds as if they were crew. Emotional beat: devotion shading into denial — she still believes someone is listening.

chapters.title: A Name That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A routine manifest sync from the derelict relay returns corrupted: the Vector and Static, a ship scrapped pre-launch, now lists Coral Lockridge as senior caretaker, signed nine years ago. She checks her own logs and finds a gap she never noticed. Emotional beat: vertigo — the first crack in the certainty of her own past.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Weather
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, intercut with recovered log fragments. She reviews her arrival records and finds her sister Wren mentioned nowhere, though Coral remembers burying her. The vault's AI, Tessel, admits its memory was pruned by external command. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion; the reader learns her memory may be edited.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following the manifest thread, she powers up the relay's deep archive and finds the Vector and Static's true flight plan: it launched in secret carrying mutineers fleeing the fleet's ration regime. Its destination: her vault. Emotional beat: dread — she has been living inside someone else's cover story.

chapters.title: Signal Debt
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Tessel reveals the pruning orders came through the edge relay, which is dying on backup power. If it fails, no one can ever verify or refute the falsified records. Coral decides she must go — a six-week crossing in a scavenged hauler. Emotional beat: resolve born of anger rather than courage.

chapters.title: Leaving the Seeds
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She seals the vault, sets the seeds to autonomous care, and records a goodbye she doesn't believe anyone will hear. Launch is rough; the hauler's drive stutters. Emotional beat: loss — leaving the only home she remembers, for a truth that may unmake her.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In transit, she intercepts fleet chatter: three ships, a brittle truce, and a countdown — the truce expires when the relay dies, taking the shared navigation clock with it. She also hears a voice using Wren's callsign. Emotional beat: hope weaponized against her; is the voice bait or her sister?

chapters.title: What the Hauler Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The hauler's black box contains partial footage of the Vector and Static's launch night — including a woman with Coral's face arguing with officers. Her implanted memories begin conflicting with what she sees. Emotional beat: dissociation; she starts narrating herself in third person.

chapters.title: Wren, Possibly
chapters.summary: POV shift: Wren aboard the fleet ship Meridian, alive, serving as the truce's reluctant enforcer. She recognizes Coral's unauthorized transmissions and realizes the vault caretaker is the sister she helped erase. Emotional beat: guilt — Wren chose the fleet's lie to keep three hundred people fed.

chapters.title: The Truce Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashbacks reveal the mutiny: the Vector and Static was real, launched by starving crew who stole seed stock — the very stock Coral guards. The fleet rewrote everyone's records to prevent war over the theft. Emotional beat: moral compromise; every survivor is both victim and accomplice.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Meridian intercepts Coral's hauler under pretense of rescue. Coral and Wren meet face to face; Wren confirms the memories were implanted to make Coral a willing custodian of the stolen seeds' alibi. Emotional beat: confrontation — love and betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: Two Versions of One Night
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Locked in quarters, she compares her implanted memories with the archive footage and reconstructs the real launch night: she chose to stay behind and take the blame so Wren could live. Emotional beat: painful reclamation — her identity survives the editing, changed but hers.

chapters.title: Course Correction
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren must log Coral as a stowaway, which will mean airlock execution under truce law. Instead she falsifies a repair detail and smuggles Coral toward the relay aboard a maintenance skiff. Emotional beat: defiance — Wren finally pays her own debt to the truth.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, alone on the skiff. Silent weeks; she grieves the lost years and rehearses what she'll broadcast. The fleet's chatter turns ugly — captains accusing each other of hoarding, the truce fraying. Emotional beat: solitude transformed into clarity about what matters.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Edge
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She reaches the relay to find its core deliberately damaged — someone wants the old records unrecoverable forever. With Tessel guiding remotely, she begins repairs with hours, not days, of life support margin. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened into focus.

chapters.title: The Countdown Clock
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The truce expires in thirty-six hours; the fleet's ships arm against each other. Wren stalls her captain with a fabricated sensor ghost while Coral fights the relay's failing systems. Emotional beat: converging tension — two sisters racing one clock from opposite ends.

chapters.title: Everything the Archive Knows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The archive comes online: full flight manifests, the mutiny record, the memory-edit orders, and proof the seed theft kept three hundred people alive. The truth indicts everyone, including Wren — and Coral herself. Emotional beat: terrible completeness; the truth offers no clean heroes.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Coral's POV. As the truce lapses and weapons arm, Coral transmits everything — then strips all names, including her own and Wren's, from the public feed, sending identified copies only to each captain privately. Ships stand down rather than fight a war whose cause is now common knowledge. Emotional beat: sacrifice — she saves them by erasing herself.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Anonymously
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fleet convenes; the anonymous broadcast forces shared accountability instead of vengeance. Wren, publicly innocent, privately carries the cost. She sends a single message toward the relay: 'Come home.' Emotional beat: bittersweet relief — justice done imperfectly, mercy undeserved.

chapters.title: The Return Crossing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She limps back toward the vault with the relay stabilized and her name officially nonexistent. She rereads her own early logs and finds she likes the woman in them — the edited one and the real one are not enemies. Emotional beat: integration — identity rebuilt from both versions.

chapters.title: Germination Tests, Year Ten
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Back at the vault, she plants the first test rows from the disputed seed stock — grown openly now, logged honestly. Wren arrives on the first sanctioned supply run in a decade. Emotional beat: quiet reconciliation; survival's price paid, its harvest finally shared.

chapters.title: Vector and Static
chapters.summary: Final chapter, dual POV closing on Coral. She restores the Vector and Static's true name to the official record and adds her own beneath it — caretaker, mutineer's sister, survivor. The last transmission goes out signed. Emotional beat: resolution — she claims the self she paid for, and signs her work.
